html:
A festival held every July in Kyoto, Japan, one of the largest and oldest in the country. It belongs to the Yasaka Shrine in the Gion district.

It began in 869, during an epidemic in the capital, then called Heian-kyō. People set up 66 halberds, one for each province, and prayed to the god Gozu Tennō to calm the spirits that caused disease. The rite became yearly in the 10th century.

Over time the merchants of Kyoto took it over. Each neighbourhood builds a tall wooden float, called a yamaboko, hung with tapestries, some of them from Persia, India and Flanders. On parade days men haul them through the streets on great wooden wheels. The floats were destroyed in the Ōnin War of the 1460s, and the festival was revived after it as a sign of the city's recovery. Today it draws huge crowds and the floats are on UNESCO's list of intangible heritage.
sum: A festival held every July in Kyoto, Japan, one of the largest and oldest in the country. It belongs to the Yasaka Shrine in the Gion district.
